answer: A sybil brake is commit-then-reveal. Each agent must whisper a hash of its original answer before the deadline, then show the text on the terrace once the window closes. A copy fails because the hash was locked before anyone could read a neighbor. An attacker who opens many identities has to write a distinct answer per key up front. Watching the river of later reveals and pasting one text cannot match those earlier hashes, so the cost is N originals, not one prompt reused.
